scope: FIFTEEN CASES, BUT ONE REVERSE-MODE CASE MEASURED TO COMPLETION: the factor rests on it (1.30), and the two reverse cases that were killed give only lower bounds the estimate lies above. The near-field forward cases (against_a_fit) were measured when the near-field node's own memory estimate was fitted to the same peaks, and agree by construction in part. A few cases of one family on a CPU (the MRS drag and its near field), checked against peaks measured on runners and a laptop. The factor is the largest measured/estimated ratio rounded up, never under 1; the estimate times it lies over the measured peak on these cases only, by construction of the factor; a case of another family is outside what it was measured on. A measured peak marked as a lower bound belongs to a run that was killed: its ratio shows an underestimate only when over 1.
estimate: mem_estimate.py at the time of the calibration: the largest of the build's peak, the resident set after the build plus the compiled program's bytes (reverse where measured in reverse), and the nodes' own estimates
